title: Capacitive Loading in Two-dimensional Fluxonium Quantum Processors
authors: Quan Guan, Guo Xuan Chan, Xu Dou, Chunqing Deng, Lijing Jin
abstract: Capacitive loading has emerged as a major obstacle to scaling fluxonium qubits from one-dimensional to highly connected two-dimensional (2D) architectures, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We derive an analytical relation between the qubit capacitance budget and the achievable capacitive coupling to external circuit elements, identifying the parasitic capacitances of Josephson junctions and Josephson junction arrays as the dominant source of capacitive loading while showing that the qubit-pad geometry can instead be engineered to mitigate it. Building on these insights, we formulate practical design principles and numerically demonstrate ultrafast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates in 2D fluxonium architectures. Our results reveal that capacitive loading does not constitute a fundamental limit for 2D fluxonium quantum processors.
summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of capacitive loading when scaling fluxonium qubits to 2D arrays. By deriving analytical models based on capacitance budgets, the authors show that this loading can be mitigated through careful geometric engineering of the qubit-coupler layout. They demonstrate that high-fidelity gates are achievable in large processors by optimizing parasitic coupling paths.
main_problem: Capacitive loading is a major obstacle preventing the scaling of fluxonium qubits from 1D to highly connected 2D architectures, and its physical origin remains poorly understood.
main_result: The authors show that capacitive loading does not constitute a fundamental limit for 2D fluxonium quantum processors if proper design principles are followed by optimizing qubit-coupler geometry.
method: They derive analytical relations and use circuit QED analysis to model the coupling strength ($J_{qc}$) based on capacitance participation ratios, comparing optimized vs. conventional layouts.
model_or_system: The system is a fluxonium quantum processor extended to 2D arrays with double-transmon couplers (DTCs). The analysis uses circuit QED principles and Hamiltonian modeling for qubit-coupler interactions.
key_observables: Achievable two-qubit gate coupling strength ($J_{qc}$), capacitive loading factors ($	ext{C}_{	ext{ab}}/	ext{C}_{	ext{eff}}^q$, $	ext{C}_{	ext{bg}}/	ext{C}_{	ext{eff}}^{	ext{bg}}$), and gate infidelity ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Capacitance budget, coupling energy ($J_{qc}$), parasitic capacitances, and the minimum physical junction size.
main_assumptions: The leakage analysis assumes that the overall leakage probability is dominated by the most dominant parasitic transition path.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate coupling geometries, show $J_{qc}$ vs. capacitance budgets comparing optimized to conventional layouts, and detail high-connectivity processor unit cells (e.g., 7q6c).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the fundamental analytical relations governing capacitive loading in simple models, to developing quantitative design principles using participation ratios, and finally demonstrating these principles on complex, high-connectivity 2D architectures while analyzing gate fidelity.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, physics-based engineering guidelines for scaling superconducting qubits by quantifying parasitic losses, which is crucial for realizing large quantum processors.
